messages.subject: broader definition of occupancy
parts:
I was wondering what the group thought about so-called "broader definitions of occupancy", where p becomes "intensity of use" and is assumed to be a product of availability and perception? (ala Ladie et al. Plos ONE 0191730). This has primarily been mentioned relative to camera trap studies involving occupancy studies.  Is that parameter useful?  Is it legitimate from a statistical standpoint?  
Thanks!
Joe
